 1        I.       WITNESS IDENTIFICATION AND PURPOSE OF SUPPLEMENTAL
 2                                      TESTIMONY
 3   Q.        Please state your name and business address.

4    A.        My name is Alexander G. Trowbridge. My business address is 3500 Blake Street,

5              Denver, Colorado 80205.

6    Q.        On whose behalf are you testifying in this proceeding?

7    A.        I am filing testimony on behalf of Southwestern Public Service Company, a New

8              Mexico corporation (“SPS”) and wholly owned electric utility subsidiary of Xcel

 9             Energy Inc (“Xcel Energy”). 1

10   Q.        Are you the same Alexander G. Trowbridge that filed direct testimony in this

11             proceeding on November 20, 2026?

12   A.        Yes.

13   Q.        Which Bench Requests will your testimony address?

14   A.        I will respond to Question Nos. NMPRC 1-(a), 1-(b), 1-(d), 1-(k) and 1-(n).




               Xcel Energy is the parent company of four utility operating companies: Northern States Power
               1

     Company, a Minnesota corporation; Northern States Power Company, a Wisconsin corporation; Public
     Service Company of Colorado, a Colorado corporation; and SPS (collectively, “Operating Companies”).
     Xcel Energy’s natural gas pipeline company is WestGas InterState, Inc.

 1        II.      WITNESS IDENTIFICATION AND PURPOSE OF SUPPLEMENTAL
 2                                      TESTIMONY

 3                                    QUESTION NO. NMPRC 1-(a):
 4   Q.         What is the number of kilowatt hours (kWh) consumed per month and (if

 5              applicable) demand (kW) metered per month, by an average-use customer

 6              within each of SPS's customer classes.

 7   A.         Attachment AGT-BR-1(a), also provided as Attachment AGT-BR-8 to the Direct

 8              Testimony of Alexander G. Trowbridge, line nos. 3 through 14, presents an

 9              approximate average-use per customer within each of SPS’s customer classes. For

10              the purpose of Attachment AGT-8, average-use represents forecasted sales, less a

11              credit to sales volumes based on community solar base rate bill credits.




                                                     2
                                      Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                    Supplemental Testimony
                                               of
                                    Alexander G. Trowbridge

 1                               QUESTION NO. NMPRC 1-(b):

 2   Q.    Please provide (a) each class of service, (b) separately for the summer and non-

 3         summer months, and (c) for various levels of use:

 4   i.    The monthly bill under current rates stating separately the customer charge,

 5         usage charge, any demand charge, the Fuel and Purchased Power Cost

 6         Adjustment Clause (FPPCAC) charge, any other separate charges (such as the

 7         renewable energy and energy efficiency rider charges) but excluding taxes and

8          surcharges and the total bill.

 9   A.    Please refer to Attachment AGT-BR-1(b)(k) for the current rates, stating separately

10         the customer charge, usage charge, any demand charge, the FPPCAC charge, and

11         other separate charges but excluding taxes and surcharges and the total bill.

12   ii.   The monthly bill under proposed rates separately stating the customer charge,

13         usage charge, any demand charge, the FPPCAC charge, any other separate

14         charges (such as the renewable energy and energy efficiency rider charges) but

15         excluding taxes and surcharges and the total bill.

16   A.    Please refer to Attachment AGT-BR-1(b)(k) for the proposed rates, stating

17         separately the customer charge, usage charge, any demand charge, the FPPCAC

 1        charge, and other separate charges but excluding taxes and surcharges and the total

 2        bill.

 3                               QUESTION NO. NMPRC 1-(d):

 4   Q.   What is SPS's approved non-fuel revenue requirement in Case No. 22-00287-

 5        UT?

 6   A.   SPS is assuming that the Commission is referring to Case No. 22-00286-UT, which

 7        is SPS’s most recently approved base rate case. That case was settled via Contested

 8        Comprehensive Stipulation. It was a “black box” settlement and there was no

 9        stipulated or approved non-fuel revenue requirement.          The Certification of

10        Stipulation that was approved by the Commission called for a $33.0 million base

11        rate revenue increase. Exhibit A of the Stipulation includes an illustrative cost of

12        service that provides for total settled base rate revenues of $507,322,504.




                                               4
                                     Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                   Supplemental Testimony
                                              of
                                   Alexander G. Trowbridge

 1                               QUESTION NO. NMPRC 1-(k):

 2   Q.   Please provide a break-down of the proposed revenue requirement by

 3        function, classification, cost allocation, class allocation, and rate design in

 4        accordance with the table attached to this Bench Request as Exhibit A.

 5   A.   Please refer to Attachment AGT-BR-1(b)(k) for the proposed revenue requirement

 6        by function, classification, cost allocation, class allocation, and rate design in

 7        accordance with the table attached to this Bench Request.

 8                               QUESTION NO. NMPRC 1-(n):

 9   Q.   Please provide a list of SPS regulatory assets or other items currently being

10        recovered through rate riders. An explanation of whether those existing rate

11        riders should be modified, terminated, or rolled into the rate base.

12   A.   The following table presents a list of New Mexico jurisdiction-related regulatory

13        assets or other items currently being recovered through rate riders.

14
                New Mexico Rider              Reg Asset/Liability        Modify, Terminate, or
                                                        (Y/N)                        Roll
                                                                         into Rate Base (Y/N)
           Fuel                                        Yes                        No
           Energy Efficiency                           Yes                        No
           Electric Vehicle Infrastructure             Yes                        No
           Renewable Portfolio Standard                Yes                        No
           Grid Modernization                          Yes                        Yes


                                               5
                                     Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                   Supplemental Testimony
                                              of
                                   Alexander G. Trowbridge

1         SPS has proposed to roll the cost of the Grid Modernization Rider (“GMR”) into

2         base rates and terminate the rider. SPS does not propose to modify, terminate, or

3         roll into rate base any of its other existing rider mechanisms. In this Application,

4         SPS has included the plant-related assets and any other costs associated with the

5         GMR in the Test Year revenue requirement. As discussed in the direct testimony

6         of     SPS   witness     Taylor    J.       Hurt   on   page    54,    lines   5-8,

7         “The Grid Modernization Rider is set to expire December 31, 2026, at or

8         around when new base rates are expected to take effect. In the event base rates go

 9        into effect prior to the termination of the Grid Modernization Rider, SPS

10        will terminate the Grid Modernization Rider.”

11   Q.   Does this conclude your pre-filed supplemental testimony?

12   A.   Yes.
